sections.h2: Notices Oklahoma requires before an eviction filing
sections.html:
Which notice applies depends on why the landlord wants the tenant out, and periods run from 5 days to 30 days. The Oklahoma Residential Landlord and Tenant Act in Title 41 sets them, while the court case itself follows Title 12, Sections 1148.1 and following.

A landlord who gets the notice wrong usually has to start over, and that costs weeks. For an owner planning a sale, a rental that cannot be handed over empty, or with a clean lease, can stall the closing. The main notices are summarized here.

Oklahoma eviction notice periods by situation
SituationNotice periodOklahoma statute
Unpaid rent5 days after written demand41 O.S. 131(B)
Lease violation that can be curedTermination not less than 15 days after receipt, unless fixed within 10 days41 O.S. 132(B)
Repairable damage by the tenant10 days after written notice to fix it41 O.S. 132(A)
Month-to-month tenancyWritten notice at least 30 days before the end date41 O.S. 111(A)
Tenancy shorter than month-to-monthWritten notice at least 7 days before the end date41 O.S. 111(B)
Imminent, irremediable harm or criminal activityNo cure period; eviction may be filed immediately41 O.S. 132(C), (D)

sections.h2: The five-day notice for unpaid rent
sections.html:
The landlord demands the unpaid rent in writing, and the tenant has five days to pay. If the money does not arrive in that time, the landlord may end the rental agreement under 41 O.S. Section 131(B).

A demand for past-due rent also counts as a demand for possession, so no separate notice to quit is needed. The landlord can send the demand before or after suing for the rent, and may sue for the rent at any point after it comes due.

Nonpayment is the fastest road to possession in the Act. If you are selling, know that a tenant who pays within the five days shuts that road.

sections.h2: When a tenant breaks the lease in another way
sections.html:
The landlord serves a written notice naming the violation. The lease ends no sooner than 15 days after the tenant receives it, unless the tenant fixes the problem within 10 days. This is 41 O.S. Section 132(B).

  • If the problem can be repaired, replaced or cleaned, the tenant has 10 days after written notice, or less if an emergency demands it.
  • If the tenant does nothing, the landlord may enter, do the work and bill the actual and reasonable cost as rent.
  • A landlord who makes the repair may not terminate the lease over that violation.
  • A later violation can support immediate termination on written notice.
  • Conduct that threatens imminent and irremediable harm, or criminal activity that endangers others or the property, allows an eviction filing with no cure period.

Section 132 also names drug-related criminal activity on or near the premises, by the tenant, a household member, a guest or anyone under the tenant's control, as grounds for immediate termination.

Either side can end a month-to-month or at-will tenancy by serving written notice at least 30 days before the termination date. Section 41-111 sets this rule, and it is the usual route when an owner simply wants the house back.

A fixed-term lease ends on its end date with no notice, unless it was ended early under the Act or by agreement. If the tenant stays on without the landlord's consent, the landlord may sue right away for possession and damages. A willful holdover that is not in good faith can add up to twice the average monthly rent, prorated daily. If the landlord agrees to let the tenant stay, a month-to-month tenancy results unless the parties agreed otherwise.

The statute also covers service. Personal delivery comes first. If the tenant cannot be found, the notice may go to a household member over 12 who lives there, or be posted on the unit with a copy sent by certified mail or through the Firm Mailing Book for Accountable Mail.

Section 41-111(G) says the notice rules do not apply to an occupant who has no rental agreement and whose tenancy the landlord never agreed to. The landlord may tell that person to leave without eviction proceedings.

If the person does not leave within a reasonable time, the statute treats it as a trespass punishable by a fine of up to $500. That is different from a tenant who once had permission, so check the facts before choosing a path.

sections.h2: The court process after the notice period
sections.html:
The landlord files a forcible entry and detainer action in district court, and the court clerk prepares the affidavit that starts the case and the summons. Under 12 O.S. Section 1148.14, an action within small claims limits goes on the small claims docket of the district court.

  • Summons form: a plain-language form developed by the Oklahoma Bar Association, available through the Oklahoma State Courts Network.
  • Hearing date: at least five days after the summons is issued, with the summons delivered at least three days before the hearing (12 O.S. 1148.16). Section 1148.5 repeats the three-day rule for service.
  • Title disputes: a defendant who files an affidavit about title or a boundary has 10 days after filing to answer (12 O.S. 1148.6).
  • After judgment: a motion for new trial is due within three days and does not stop execution. The writ tells the sheriff to remove the defendant and give the plaintiff possession (12 O.S. 1148.10).

The clerk at the district court where the rental sits is the best contact for filing fees, forms and hearing dates.

sections.h2: Eviction timing when you want to sell a rental
sections.html:
If the buyer wants the house empty, the notice period and the court dates set the earliest realistic closing. A five-day notice followed by a hearing at least five days after summons is the shortest path in the statutes. A 30-day month-to-month notice before filing adds a month.

The Act also limits what a lease can contain. Under 41 O.S. Section 113, a lease cannot make the tenant give up rights under the Act, permit a confession of judgment, require the tenant to pay the landlord's attorney fees, or limit the right to call for emergency help. Terms like those are unenforceable, so a landlord should not count on them to speed things up.

For the effect of a sale on an existing lease, read the lease itself and ask an Oklahoma attorney before promising a buyer an empty house. An owner who would rather not wait on a tenant can ask about an as-is offer for the house.

sections.h2: Records to keep before sending any notice
sections.html: Keep a simple file from the start: the lease, the rent ledger, the date and method of delivery for every notice, and photographs of any damage. If the case reaches court, those papers answer most of the judge's questions, and if a buyer asks about the tenant's history, they are what you hand over.

faqs.q: How many days notice does an Oklahoma landlord give for unpaid rent?
faqs.a: Five days after written demand. If the tenant does not pay within five days, the landlord may terminate under 41 O.S. Section 131(B) without a separate notice to quit.

faqs.q: How much notice ends a month-to-month tenancy?
faqs.a: Written notice at least 30 days before the termination date, from either landlord or tenant, under 41 O.S. Section 111(A).

faqs.q: What is the notice for a lease violation?
faqs.a: Written notice that the lease ends not less than 15 days after receipt, unless the tenant fixes the violation within 10 days, under 41 O.S. Section 132(B).

faqs.q: How soon can an eviction hearing be held?
faqs.a: At least five days after the summons is issued, and the summons must be delivered at least three days before the hearing, under 12 O.S. Section 1148.16.

faqs.q: Can a landlord remove a tenant without going to court, or sell with a tenant in place?
faqs.a: A tenant with a rental agreement cannot be removed without a court writ carried out by the sheriff. A house with a tenant can be sold, but the lease and notice rules still apply: a fixed-term lease ends on its end date, and a month-to-month tenancy needs 30 days written notice from the landlord.
